source_text: Ὅλως δὲ κἂν συγχωρήσῃ τις τὴν ἐκ τούτων εἰσιοῦσαν τροφήν (προσειρήσθω δὲ τοῦτο συνηθέστερον), καίπερ οὖσαν παρὰ φύσιν, διακρίνεσθαι καὶ ματαβάλλειν εἰς ἕν τι τῶν ὑγραινόντων ἢ ξηραινόντων ἢ θερμαινόντων ἢ ψυχόντων, οὐδ᾿ οὕτως ἐκ τῶν συγχωρηθέντων αὐτοῖς γενήσεταί τι προὔργου, τῶν μὲν ἀνισταμένων σωμάτων ἐκ τῶν οἰκείων μερῶν πάλιν συνισταμένων, οὐδενὸς δὲ τῶν εἰρημένων μέρους ὄντος, οὐδὲ τὴν ὡς μέρους ἐπέχοντος σχέσιν ἢ τάξιν, οὐ μὴν οὐδὲ παραμένοντος πάντοτε τοῖς τρεφομένοις τοῦ σώματος μέρεσιν, ἢ συνανισταμένου τοῖς ἀνισταμένοις, οὐδὲν συντελοῦντος ἔτι πρὸς τὸ ζῆν οὐχ αἵματος οὐ φλέγματος οὐ χολῆς οὐ πνεύματος. οὐδὲ γὰρ ὧν ἐδεήθη ποτὲ τὰ τρεφόμενα σώματα, δεηθήσεται καὶ τότε, συνανῃρημένης τῇ τῶν τρεφομένων ἐνδείᾳ καὶ φθορᾷ τῆς ἐξ ὧν ἐτρέφετο χρείας. ἔπειτ' εἰ καὶ μέχρι σαρκὸς φθάνειν τὴν ἐκ τῆς τοιαύτης τροφῆς μεταβολὴν ὑποθοῖτό τις, οὐδ' οὕτως ἀνάγκη τις ἔσται τὴν νεωστὶ μεταβληθεῖσαν ἐκ τῆς τοιᾶσδε τροφῆς σάρκα προσπελάσασαν ἑτέρου τινὸς ἀνθρώπου σώματι πάλιν ὡς μέρος εἰς τὴν ἐκείνου τελεῖν συμπλήρωσιν, τῷ μήτε αὐτὴν τὴν προσλαμβάνουσαν σάρκα πάντοτε φυλάττειν ἣν προσείληφεν, μήτε τὴν ἑνωθεῖσαν ταύτην μόνιμον εἶναι καὶ παραμένειν παραμένειν τοῖς μέρεσιν ἃ συνδεῖν ἢ στέγειν ἢ θάλπειν πέφυκεν τὴν ὑπὸ τῆς φύσεως ἐξειλεγμένην καὶ τούτοις προσπεφυκυῖαν οἷς τὴν κατὰ φύσιν συνεξέπλησε ζωὴν καὶ τοὺς ἐν τῇ ζωῇ πόνους. Ἀλλ᾿ οὔτε γὰρ καθ᾿ ὃ δεῖ κρινομένων τῶν ἔναγχος ἐξητασμένων, οὔτε κατὰ συγχώρησιν παραδεχθέντων τῶν ἐπ᾿ ἐκείνοις γεγυμνασμένων, ἀληθὲς δεικνύναι δυνατὸν τὸ πρὸς αὐτῶν λεγόμενον, οὔτ᾿ ἂν συγκραθείη ποτὲ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων σώματα τοῖς τῆς αὐτῆς οὖσι φύσεως, κἂν ὑπ᾿ ἀγνοίας ποτὲ κλαπῶσι τὴν αἴσθησιν δι᾿ ἑτέρου τινὸς μετασχόντες τοιούτου σώματος, κἂν αὐτόθεν ὑπ᾿ ἐνδείας ἢ μανίας ὁμοειδοῦς τινος μιανθῶσι σώματι· εἴ γε μὴ λελήθασιν ἡμᾶς ἀνθρωποειδεῖς τινες ὄντες θῆρες, ἢ μικτὴν ἔχοντες φύσιν ἐξ ἀνθρώπων καὶ θηρίων, οἵους πλάττειν εἰώθασιν οἱ τολμηρότεροι τῶν ποιητῶν.
thought_title: Even if such food changed, it would not become part of the risen body
orientation: Athenagoras is answering the objection that human bodies eaten by other humans could be raised, by arguing that even if such food were somehow changed, it would not become a permanent part of the body that is raised.
pass_a_gloss: But wholly even if someone should concede the food entering from these [things] (and let this be said more customarily), although being contrary to nature, to be separated and to change into one of the moistening or drying or heating or cooling [things], not even thus from the things conceded to them will anything of advantage come to be, the bodies being raised being composed again from their own parts, and none of the things mentioned being a part, nor holding the relation or order as of a part, nor indeed remaining always with the parts of the body being nourished, or being raised together with the things being raised, contributing nothing still to living, not of blood, not of phlegm, not of bile, not of breath. For neither of the things which the bodies being nourished once needed will they need also then, the need of the things from which it was nourished having been destroyed together with the lack and corruption of the things being nourished. Then even if someone should suppose the change from such food to reach as far as flesh, not even thus will there be any necessity that the flesh newly changed from such food, having approached the body of some other human, again as a part complete the completion of that one, because neither does the flesh that receives it always keep what it has received, nor is this [flesh] that has been united permanent and remain remaining with the parts which to bind or to cover or to warm has been naturally fitted the [flesh] selected by nature and grown to these [parts] with which it completed the life according to nature and the labors in life. But neither for according to what is necessary the things just examined being judged, nor according to concession the things exercised upon those being accepted, is it possible to show true the thing said by them, nor would ever the bodies of humans be mixed with those being of the same nature, even if through ignorance they should ever steal the perception, having shared through some other such body, even if from there through lack or madness they should be defiled by a body of the same kind; if indeed human-shaped beasts have not escaped our notice, or having a mixed nature from humans and beasts, such as the bolder of the poets are accustomed to fashion.

choices.english: and let this be said in the more customary way
choices.why: The parenthetical remark concedes the common way of speaking about food entering the body, even though strictly it is contrary to nature.
rejected: and let this be said more habitually
and let this be said more conventionally

choices.term: οὐδ᾿ οὕτως ἐκ τῶν συγχωρηθέντων αὐτοῖς γενήσεταί τι προὔργου
choices.english: not even so will anything useful come to them from what has been granted
choices.why: προὔργου means 'of advantage' or 'useful'; the concessive force of 'not even so' is essential to the argument.
rejected: not even so will anything of profit arise for them
not even so will anything of benefit be produced for them

choices.term: οὐδενὸς δὲ τῶν εἰρημένων μέρους ὄντος
choices.english: and none of the things mentioned being a part
choices.why: The genitive absolute preserves the causal/explanatory force: since none of the things mentioned is a part.
rejected: and none of the things mentioned being of a part
and none of the things mentioned being a portion

choices.term: οὐδὲ τὴν ὡς μέρους ἐπέχοντος σχέσιν ἢ τάξιν
choices.english: nor holding the relation or order as of a part
choices.why: σχέσις ἢ τάξις means 'relation or order'; the phrase 'as of a part' preserves the ὡς + genitive construction.
rejected: nor occupying the position or order of a part
nor having the relation or arrangement as a part

choices.term: συνανῃρημένης τῇ τῶν τρεφομένων ἐνδείᾳ καὶ φθορᾷ τῆς ἐξ ὧν ἐτρέφετο χρείας
choices.english: the need for the things from which it was nourished having been destroyed along with the lack and corruption of the things that are nourished
choices.why: The genitive absolute is complex; 'having been destroyed along with' captures συνανῃρημένης, and the dative τῇ ἐνδείᾳ καὶ φθορᾷ is rendered as 'along with the lack and corruption'.
rejected: the use of the things from which it was nourished having been taken away together with the lack and corruption of the things nourished

choices.term: τὴν ὑπὸ τῆς φύσεως ἐξειλεγμένην καὶ τούτοις προσπεφυκυῖαν
choices.english: the flesh selected by nature and grown to these parts
choices.why: ἐξειλεγμένην is perfect passive participle of ἐκλέγω, 'selected'; προσπεφυκυῖαν is perfect participle of προσφύω, 'grown to, attached to'.
rejected: the flesh chosen by nature and attached to these
the flesh picked out by nature and clinging to these

pass_b_english: But suppose someone grants that the food entering from these bodies, and let this be said in the more customary way, even though it is contrary to nature, is separated and transformed into one of the moistening, drying, heating, or cooling substances. Even so, nothing useful will come to them from what has been granted. The bodies that are raised are composed again from their own proper parts, and none of the things mentioned is a part, nor does it hold the relation or order of a part. Nor does it always remain with the parts of the body that are nourished, nor is it raised together with the bodies that are raised, since it no longer contributes anything to life: not blood, not phlegm, not bile, not breath. For the bodies that are nourished will not need then what they once needed, because the need for the things from which they were nourished is destroyed along with the lack and corruption of the things that are nourished.

Then, even if someone supposes that the change from such food reaches as far as flesh, there will still be no necessity that the flesh newly changed from such food, having approached another human being's body, should again serve as a part to complete that body. For the flesh that receives it does not always preserve what it has received, nor is the flesh united to it permanent and remaining with the parts which by nature bind, cover, or warm the flesh selected by nature and grown to those parts, the flesh with which nature completed the life according to nature and the labors in that life.

But neither when the matters just examined are judged as they should be, nor when the arguments developed against them are accepted by concession, is it possible to show that what is said by them is true. Nor could the bodies of human beings ever be blended with bodies of the same human nature, even if through ignorance they are ever robbed of perception by sharing in another such body, even if they are defiled on the spot by a body of the same kind through lack or madness. Unless, of course, we have failed to notice that there are certain human-shaped beasts, or beings with a mixed nature from humans and animals, such as the bolder poets are accustomed to invent.

last_rejected.quote: the lack and corruption of the things that are nourished
last_rejected.source_quote: τῇ τῶν τρεφομένων ἐνδείᾳ καὶ φθορᾷ
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'lack and corruption OF THE THINGS NOURISHED' (genitive), not 'of the things that are nourished' modifying 'need'. The need is destroyed along with the nourished things' lack and corruption.
last_rejected.fix: because the need for the things from which they were nourished is destroyed along with the lack and corruption of the nourished things
last_rejected.ruling: Both renderings are grammatically equivalent: 'things nourished' = 'things that are nourished' (passive participle). No meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: the flesh selected by nature and grown to those parts
last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν ὑπὸ τῆς φύσεως ἐξειλεγμένην καὶ τούτοις προσπεφυκυῖαν
last_rejected.why: Subject misidentified: 'flesh' is object, not subject; nature selected and attached flesh to parts.
last_rejected.fix: the flesh nature has selected and attached to those parts
last_rejected.ruling: τὴν...σάρκα governs ἐξειλεγμένην καὶ προσπεφυκυῖαν; 'flesh selected by nature and grown to those parts' correctly renders the participles.

last_rejected.why: Missing object: 'completed for them their natural life' or 'the life natural to them'.
last_rejected.fix: the life natural to them and the toils of that life
last_rejected.ruling: τὴν κατὰ φύσιν...ζωὴν = 'the life according to nature'; no missing object, phrase is self-contained.

last_rejected.quote: robbed of perception by sharing in another such body
last_rejected.source_quote: κλαπῶσι τὴν αἴσθησιν δι᾿ ἑτέρου τινὸς μετασχόντες τοιούτου σώματος
last_rejected.why: Agency confused: critics' senses are deceived, not they robbed of perception; 'sharing' should be 'partaking'.
last_rejected.fix: deceived in perception by partaking of another such body
last_rejected.ruling: κλαπῶσι τὴν αἴσθησιν = 'robbed of perception'; μετασχόντες can mean 'sharing/partaking'; rendering captures sense adequately.

problems.quote: even if through ignorance they are ever robbed of perception by sharing in another such body
problems.why: Syntax is tangled; meaning is unclear as English.
problems.fix: Rephrase for clarity: 'even if they lose awareness by consuming another human body'.

edits.old: even if through ignorance they are ever robbed of perception by sharing in another such body
edits.new: even if through ignorance they ever lose awareness by sharing in another such body

fixed: Rephrased 'robbed of perception' to 'lose awareness' for clarity; the source κλαπῶσι τὴν αἴσθησιν means 'steal the perception/sensation,' and 'lose awareness' conveys this more naturally in English.

polish.changed: Clarified ambiguous phrases such as 'same nature' to 'same human nature,' made the final conditional sentence clearer, and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Reader cannot tell if this is a mythological or philosophical reference.
notes.fix: Add a note on the philosophical topos of human-beast hybrids.

notes.quote: nor could the bodies of human beings ever be blended with those of the same nature
notes.why: Ambiguous: 'same nature' could mean same species or same kind.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'with other human bodies of the same nature.'
